question.text: Under the PIT Regulations 2015, an "insider" is defined as:

answer.text: Any person who is or was connected with the company, or anyone who possesses or has access to UPSI
Only the directors and promoters of the company
Only those who are officially designated as insiders by the company

explanation.text: The Logic: Under general Indian securities-law principles, the PIT Regulations 2015 define an "insider" broadly to include (1) any connected person — such as directors, employees, advisors, auditors and others with a business or contractual relationship to the company — and (2) any person who is in possession of or has access to UPSI. The definition is based on possession of, or access to, UPSI rather than formal designation; even a recipient of an informal tip can fall within it. The Trap: Insider status is not limited to directors or promoters, is not confined to employees, and does not depend on the company formally labelling someone as an insider. Possession or access to UPSI is the operative test. Note: The exact PIT 2015 definition of "insider", "connected person", and UPSI is not laid out in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages; the explanation above reflects general PIT-regulation knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
